title: Event-driven QA pipelines for model version pins and upgrades (catalog + customer pins)
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Implement an event-driven QA pipeline that automatically runs targeted quality checks and smoke suites whenever a model version is pinned or upgraded, for both catalog-managed models and customer-pinned models. This ticket covers orchestration rules, trigger filters, scope scoping (catalog vs customer), cost controls, and integration points with the existing eval runner and dashboarding stack.

Background: Teams currently rely on ad-hoc preflight evals and manual canaries when moving pins in the catalog or when customers request pinned upgrades. This leads to inconsistent coverage, delayed rollouts, and occasional regressions surfacing in production. We want a standard, observable workflow that: (a) runs a lightweight smoke suite immediately on pin/upgrade, (b) enqueues targeted delta-evals for higher-sensitivity tests based on model diffs and dataset fingerprints, and (c) surfaces results with clear pass/fail and remediation actions in the Console.

Scope & non-goals: In scope: trigger rules, cost/time budgets, eval selection heuristics, rollout gating integration, and Console surface for results and automatic rollback triggers. Out of scope: building new large-scale benchmark datasets and full retraining pipelines. Hardware autoscaling and runtime kernel changes are handled in separate ENG tickets.

Success metrics: 
- 95% of catalog pin/upgrades trigger a smoke eval within 90s of the event.
- Mean time from pin event to alert (for failing smoke) < 5 minutes.
- False positive rate for auto-blocked pins < 3% (measured over first 2 months).
- Observability: every triggered run should be queryable in Console with token-level cost and run artifacts.

Artefacts & references: 
- Design doc / runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/QA-Pipelines-Event-Driven
- Eval runner PR (prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-runner/pull/489
- Console mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-ui-mockups
- Incident notes referencing regression from untested pin: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2025

Constraints & trade-offs: 
- Cost vs coverage: we will run a two-tier approach (smoke -> targeted delta-evals) to limit cost exposure for large catalog updates.
- Latency vs thoroughness: smoke suites must be tiny (<30s run time) to avoid blocking fast-rollouts; deeper delta-evals run asynchronously with clear gating windows.
- Customer pinned models: offer opt-out for customers who do not want auto-runs in their accounts (compliance/customer preference).

Design decisions made so far: 
1) Trigger model: event broker (Kafka) emits pin/upgrade events; a lambda-like orchestrator enqueues smoke runs immediately and marks ticket with run_id.
2) Eval selection: use model diff heuristics (tokenizer changes, architecture changes, quantization change) to pick targeted eval suites.
3) Budgeting: per-event budget cap with fallback that degrades to a minimal smoke only when budgets are exceeded.
4) Rollout gating: failures in smoke can optionally block the pin if the pin was initiated by automated catalog promotions; for customer-initiated pins we surface but do not auto-block unless customer opted-in.

Open questions: 
- What is the definitive list of features in the smoke suite? (PM, SRE, and Research to agree)
- Should we store raw eval artifacts in long term storage by default, or only preserve summaries?
- How to present multi-run deltas in Console for a customer with many pins in a short time window?

Next steps / acceptance criteria: 
- Orchestrator can subscribe to pin events and create a run_id (proof-of-concept).
- Smoke suite defined (<= 10 checks) and implemented in eval-runner prototype.
- Console shows run status and results with links to artifacts for a test catalog and a test customer.
- Config knobs for per-catalog/per-customer opt-out and budget caps.

Acceptance criteria (explicit):
- "Smoke" trigger executes within 90s for pinned events in our test harness and reports PASS/FAIL.
- For a patched model with a deliberate regression on stop-phrase handling, a delta-eval catches the regression and flags the pin in the Console.
- Rollout policy respects the customer opt-out flag and logs the decision in audit trail.
